title: Structural and regulatory evolution across the genus Hordeum
summary:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11332-7

Chromosome-scale pangenomics across diploid Hordeum species reveals extensive structural variation, hybridization, introgression, horizontal gene transfer and regulatory evolution, revealing adaptive trait diversification and providing genomic resources for barley improvement.

title: Host–microbe interactions in engineered immunocompetent human gut tissues
summary:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11292-y

Engineered barrier models of the small intestine and colon that include immune cells and a microbial compartment enable characterizations of the human epithelial response to Salmonella Typhimurium at the single-cell level.

title: Ferroptosis in cancer cells triggers PGE<sub>2</sub> production for tumour immune escape
summary:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11333-6

Ferroptotic cancer cells activate a molecular program that causes increased levels of PGE2, which in turn impairs type 1 conventional dendritic cell function, compromising antitumour CD8+ T cell immunity.

title: Hypothalamic volume and cell-type changes in ageing and Alzheimer’s disease
summary:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11305-w

HypoAD, an atlas of the human hypothalamus in ageing and Alzheimer’s disease that combines high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging from 458 individuals with single-nucleus RNA sequencing of 614,403 nuclei, reveals that metabolism- and circadian-regulating subregions, and their inhibitory neurons and microglia, are particularly vulnerable.

title: Tropical land-use intensification restructures biodiversity
summary:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11298-6

Tropical land-use intensification drives substantial biodiversity loss and reorganizes community composition, with aboveground assemblages showing an increase in nestedness in monocultures compared with forests, underscoring the need for landscape-scale, multi-taxon conservation that integrates agricultural and natural habitats.

title: Conservation of the tumour microenvironment across organs and species
summary:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11270-4

A pan-cancer single-cell analysis of the tumour microenvironment across 42 cancer types and across 2 species is described.

title: TransA-MERFISH reveals divergent post-retinal direction-selective circuits
summary:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11235-7

TransA-MERFISH combines anterograde trans-neuronal tracing and spatial transcriptomics and reveals distinct retinal on–off direction-selective ganglion cell-dependent and independent motion-selective pathways in superior colliculus, establishing a sensitive cell-type-resolved framework for wiring-diagram reconstruction in early visual processing.

title: Closest relatives of poxviruses prevail in human and animal guts worldwide
summary:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11283-z

A diversified group of DNA viruses with large linear genomes is discovered, egoviruses, that comprise a putative viral order most closely related to animal-infecting poxviruses, and prevail in the animal digestive system.

title: Evidence for p-wave magnetism in electronic band structure of metallic EuSi
summary:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11295-9

A combination of symmetry analysis, first-principles calculations, neutron scattering and photoemission spectroscopy shows p-wave magnetism in the near-Fermi-level electronic structure of stoichiometric metallic EuSi.

title: Injury-induced signalling coordinates immunity and cannibalism in locusts
summary:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11297-7

Studies in migratory locusts identify a dual role of volatile guaiacol emission, enhancing survival of individual insects following minor injury but attracting cannibalistic attack once an injury severity threshold has been exceeded.

title: An inspiral of a star inside a common envelope with its giant companion
summary:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11221-z

Observations of AT 2025abao provide direct evidence of common-envelope inspiral, revealing frictional energy dissipation and constraining how orbital energy drives stellar-envelope ejection during binary evolution.

title: Global patterns and drivers of bee richness and endemism on islands
summary:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11325-6

Gobal analysis of bee species across 305 islands reveals that islands account for 20% of global bee diversity, with more than 4,100 species and high levels of endemism, and shows that richness is shaped by island size, isolation and evolutionary diversification.

title: Designing dislocation-driven polar vortex networks in twisted perovskites
summary:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11330-9

Experimental and theoretical investigation of twisted freestanding SrTiO3 layers using various analytic methods from 4DSTEM to DFT reveal a long-range ordered screw dislocation pattern as well as topological polar vortex arrays in the interface plane.

title: Evidence for late Middle Pleistocene Homo erectus in mainland East Asia
summary:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11271-3

Late Middle Pleistocene hominin teeth from the Naxian and Baxian caves of southern China, dated to around 324–184 thousand years ago, fill a gap in the geographical and chronological distribution of Homo erectus in East Asia.

title: Bogong moths navigate with a light-dependent geomagnetic inclination compass
summary:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11322-9

During their biannual migration, nocturnal Bogong moths (Agrotis infusa) rely on both a stellar and a geomagnetic compass for navigation, enabling them to maintain their migratory direction even if one of these cues is missing.

title: Rainforest adaptation in late Homo erectus from southern China
summary:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11155-6

Eight Homo erectus teeth from two caves in southern China reveal that the species persisted in closed rainforest ecosystems between 324 and 184 ka, challenging assumptions about their ecological preferences and behavioural limitations.

title: Transient contacts between filaments impart its elasticity to branched actin
summary:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11300-1

Stiffness of branched actin networks emerges from the formation of contacts between filaments, with growth under load resulting in stiffer networks.

title: Analogue simulation of massive relativistic quantum fields in 2 + 1 dimensions
summary:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11268-y

Analogue simulation of massive relativistic quantum fields in 2 + 1 dimensions (two spatial dimensions and time) is realized using two coherently coupled spin components in a two-dimensional atomic Bose–Einstein condensate.

title: Quantum resistance paradox of low-dimensional superfluids
summary:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11294-w

A defect-free unitary Fermi gas is used in a digitally programmable transport geometry to isolate geometric effects on superfluid dissipation and discover a paradox.

title: Flat-band-induced integer doping and phase transition in monolayer graphene
summary:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11254-4

An architecture comprising monolayer graphene doubly aligned to bulk and monolayer hBN on either side shows a gate-tunable global structural phase transition between two stacking configurations, accompanied by flat-band-induced integer doping.

title: Fully integrated perovskite active polaritonic circuits
summary:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11299-5

A fully integrated perovskite polaritonic circuit that brings the functionalities of fully integrated on-chip polaritonic systems simultaneously delivering room-temperature waveguide lasing, controllable optical routing and amplification together in a single-step-grown platform is shown.

title: Observation of tunable superradiant frequency combs
summary:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11289-7

A transition from continuous to periodic pulsed superradiant emission in coupled spin–resonator systems is demonstrated, revealing connections to time crystals and enabling synchronized microwave and optical frequency combs.

title: Widespread deciduousness reveals diverse Amazonian phenological strategies
summary:

A basin-wide assessment of Amazonian deciduousness using high-resolution satellite observations shows a diverse range of phenological strategies across the Amazon rainforest, contrary to the prevailing view of Amazonian phenology.

title: Quantum position verification with remote untrusted devices
summary:
Nature, Published online: 18 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11247-3

A loophole-free Bell-test quantum protocol demonstrates secure, device-independent position verification, achieving up to 4.53-fold smaller localization volumes than classical methods and enabling tamper-resistant location-based authentication.

title: A glucose-powered artificial neuroimmune axis for metabolic control
summary:

NeuroAxis restores glucose tolerance, improves insulin sensitivity and normalizes glycaemic control, with therapeutic effects persisting after treatment cessation in rat models of type 1 and type 2 diabetes.

The move to expand the Chinese firm’s already large contract with Microsoft has drawn the ire of OpenAI. The AI company has complained to Microsoft in recent months that it believes Chinese firms are “distilling” its AI, or running OpenAI models to create their own competing AI models, according to the people with knowledge of the discussions. OpenAI itself prevents most Chinese firms from using its AI, but Microsoft—which has the rights to sell OpenAI’s technology—doesn’t impose the same restrictions.

title: The Future of Nvidia Is About More Than AI Chips
summary:
EXPERT PERSPECTIVE — Nvidia’s board announced that Jensen Huang had resigned 33 years after he co-founded the company.

What happens to a company when a visionary CEO is gone? Too often, innovation fades and the company coasts for years on momentum and its brand. Rarely does it regain its former glory.

That’s the danger facing Nvidia — and the challenge its board must confront.

Huang reinvented Nvidia three times. In 2006, he launched CUDA, turning a graphics chip for PC gamers into a general-purpose computing platform — and funded it for years ahead of any revenue. In 2012, when researchers used Nvidia chips to win the ImageNet contest, he pointed the company toward deep learning. In 2020, with the acquisition of Mellanox, Nvidia went from selling boards with GPUs to selling integrated racks that power AI data centers.

He wasn’t one of the most famous tech billionaires – I’d never heard of him, although I used his communications platform every day. Nonetheless, it was exciting to get up close to someone that staggeringly rich to see if he was different from the rest of us.

And he was different, sort of. Leaning back in his chair, he seemed to suggest, in a bored kind of way, that in the event of a US standoff with Russia, Putin nuking London would be the sort of collateral damage Washington could tolerate. A bit of an odd thing to say to a stranger. He didn’t observe the usual rules of conversation but rather, like a Roman emperor waiting to be entertained, remained belligerently aloof.

title: The Man Who Broke Reality by Philip Ball review – the inspirational genius of Niels Bohr
summary:
Scientific discoveries are effortlessly explained in this portrait of a man whose research was driven by passion

Niels Bohr shares with Albert Einstein pride of place in the pantheon of 20th-century science. The two had much in common. They were not expert mathematicians; they prized physical intuition over mere competence; and they did not shy away from the moral and political implications of their work.

But Bohr differed from Einstein in one crucial respect: his extraordinary personality. In his gripping biography Philip Ball ensures we feel the intense pull of Bohr’s genius. Today he would probably be considered neurodivergent; he possessed a passion for physics that cast a spell on all who knew him. Solving problems is the raison d’etre of any scientist, but Bohr went far beyond that: having inaugurated quantum mechanics with his model of the atom in 1913, he simply would not give up until the rest of it was understood.

Vladimir Putin’s politics were defined then, as now, by vengeful resentment of his country’s relegation from superpower status after the cold war. His worldview is warped by a paranoid conviction that Nato never stopped striving to deepen that humiliation, even after the USSR had unravelled. From his Kremlin throne, the Russian president expects to be treated as a colossus of world history. It is hard to overstate how bitterly he hated being dismissed by Obama as a geopolitical B-lister.

Democrats will control the House and Senate in the new year, and they have a long list of priorities ahead of them. title: Would more hands-on dads create a more peaceful world? This pioneering scientist thinks so
summary:
Sarah Blaffer Hrdy unpicked Darwinian sexism to rewrite the story of evolution. Now, she’s turned her attention to the nature of fatherhood

‘Spit here, dear,” Sarah Blaffer Hrdy said to her husband, Dan, handing him a vial when he arrived in New York after the birth of the couple’s first grandchild. It was 2014 and Hrdy was conducting an experiment. Having recorded a 63% jump in oxytocin in her saliva after spending hours cuddling the baby, she wanted to find out if something similar would happen to his hormones.

It did, although it took a day longer. In her latest book, Father Time: A Natural History of Men and Babies, Hrdy records with justified pride that “this was the first time anyone had demonstrated a bump in oxytocin levels among doting grandparents”.

title: Fossil-fuel industry accused of violating Colorado law over not disclosing drilling chemicals

The fossil-fuel industry is violating Colorado law by not disclosing which chemicals it uses in drilling, a new analysis by the FracTracker Alliance nonprofit alleges, and state records show it has used illegal or dangerous compounds while fracking.

Drilling chemicals can include xylene, toluene, benzene, Pfas, and other dangerous toxicants, industry records and literature from other regions show. A first-in-the-nation 2022 Colorado law requires fossil-fuel operators and their suppliers to make public all chemicals used in “downhole oil and gas production”. But regulators have exempted compounds used in drilling, claiming that drilling is not part of production.

title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping review – surreally awful prequel to the Katniss Everdeen era
summary:
Overwrought and boring, this nadir of a prequel to the Games’ death match saga is nothing but a cash grab for an exhausted franchise

This one has another of the series’ convoluted faux-mythic subtitles: Sunrise on the Reaping. What, “harvest dawn” not old-timey enough?

Well, “reaping” in fact refers to an annual process by which ordinary smudgy faced, raggedy clothed people are chosen at random for compulsory participation in this futurist dystopia’s brutal, televised survival contest to the death: a bread-and-circuses nightmare with which the rulers keep the populace in a cowed and pacified state. In this Darwinian process, competitors strategically team up with (and then betray) some players against others in the short term, to stay in the game.

title: A Successful Space Race Needs More than “Competitive Supremacy”
summary:
The final frontier must be mutually beneficial for both US and Allies to be sustainable

While the demand for digital sovereignty continues to accelerate, driven by geopolitics and strategic necessity, recent announcements about space supremacy, the unqualified success of Artemis and massive industry growth have created what can only be described as excitement beyond any recent experience. The vision, potential addressable markets, technological innovation, and the challenges and opportunities ahead are significant and possibly already past the point of regulation.

But it does raise a profound question: how can the very nature of space as a highly contested domain align with the sovereign interests of both the US and its Allies? And why must these interests be protected for the benefit of the Alliance?

Given the existential nature of the outcomes, we cannot leave the question purely to fate.

Naming emotions is a core skill that most people develop as children, and it might seem like second nature. But research indicates that it’s harder than you think – about 10% of the general population have significant difficulty identifying their own emotions.

That’s why a simple tool called the feelings wheel has gained popularity in therapists’ offices and classrooms over recent years.

title: The Impossible Trilemma Hanging Over the Nvidia Crisis
summary: Tian Yang, CIO and manager of the VPX fund at Variant Perception, recently published a report called “The Sovereign Impossible Trinity” that is especially salient right now. Yang's thesis is that the US-China rivalry is exposing three main policy trade-offs: The necessity of sovereignty (which both of the great powers insist on) means that neither state can assure they can maintain the trio of guns (or the AI 'arms race'), butter (social spending), and sound money because of physical constraints, political conditions, and inflation. Given that the US-China AI arms race forms the backdrop of the upheaval at Nvidia, you can't understand Jensen Huang's resignation without considering geopolitical and global economic conditions. Yang talks to us today about why Jensen might be our era's Oppenheimer and what it means that the biggest powers in the world can't maintain sound monetary policy while also upholding defense and entitlements. (Source: Bloomberg)

What England produced for 65 minutes was extraordinary. What followed was equally so for different reasons. When it was over, England had made the most sensational of statements. Back in 2018, on their previous visit to Spain, England won 3-2 in Seville in the Nations League; it was one of Sir Gareth Southgate’s most famous results, an ignition point. Serving for the first set at 5-4, Andreeva nervously opened the game with two dire double faults before spraying two further unforced errors to hand over the break.

There have already been many times in Andreeva’s young career when similar sequences triggered epic, dramatic collapses, so prone the 19-year-old has been to losing her composure when things do not go her way. This time, she betrayed no negative emotions at all. Andreeva immediately retrieved the break and regained her momentum as she marched to a monumental victory, defeating Elina Svitolina 7-5, 6-3 to win the WTA Finals at Indian Wells for the first time.
